scene.name: Ball rolling down a wedge ramp onto a floor
assumptions: The attached canvas drawing is modeled at the confirmed maximum scale of 500 pixels per meter. The drawn incline is approximately 629 pixels long, so its modeled length is about 1.26 m, rather than the earlier 1 m note.
The ramp is approximated as a straight, solid triangular-prism wedge. Its drawn incline corresponds to about 1.06 m horizontal run, 0.684 m rise, and 33 degrees above horizontal.
The note specifies that the ball rests at the top of the ramp, so it is initialized in contact near the upper end even though the sketched ball is visibly separated from the ramp.
The stated 0.3 m third-dimension width is used for the ramp and ball; the floor is assumed to have the same depth.
Friction coefficients are assumed, not measured. A coefficient of 1.0 is used to permit rolling without slipping; restitution is set to zero.
Bodies are rigid. The ramp and floor are fixed, and there is no air drag or powered actuation. The wedge and flat floor are approximate collision geometry.

sources.reference: Canvas drawing and user notes/clarifications, source ebe1290a-8c88-48e9-865c-526724a881dd revision 11

grounding.note: Ball outline; modeled as the stated 0.29 m sphere and positioned in contact near the ramp top per the notes.
Vertical back and sloping outline inform a solid triangular-prism wedge; incline length is calibrated from the drawing at 500 px/m.
Separate fixed flat floor modeled from the lower outline, meeting the ramp at its lower end.

warnings: The drawing's incline calibrates to approximately 1.26 m at the confirmed 500 px/m scale; this supersedes the earlier 1 m estimate as requested.
The drawn ball is not shown touching the ramp. Its initial contact placement follows the explicit note that it rests at the ramp's top.
message: Modeled the separately fixed floor and solid triangular wedge, with the 0.5 kg ball initially resting near the upper end of the incline.
